research_question: Does source-derived SEMA expert expansion improve continual VQA accuracy and reduce forgetting relative to sequential shared-adapter tuning?
backbone: Vicuna-7B-v1.5 + CLIP ViT-L/14-336 + LLaVA-1.5 stage-one projector
decision: Support requires positive mean paired AP gain and lower mean paired AF across all three seeds on both declared protocols; report seed spread, all task matrices and exceptions. Small-subset findings are POC evidence, not full-paper reproduction or statistical proof.
selection_policy: No test-set threshold, checkpoint, task-order or hyperparameter selection; report negative results unchanged.
compute_caveat: SEMA's source-derived shallow-to-deep expansion retrains the current task after each triggered layer (up to three functional passes); sequential and simultaneous forced-expansion controls use one pass. These are not compute-matched controls, so a positive POC does not by itself isolate capacity from additional optimization.
adaptations: Transfer SEMA modular adapters from ViT to the final three multimodal language-transformer MLPs; earlier blocks have no adapters.
Pool image/question context only, excluding answer tokens to prevent target leakage.
Use released task partitions; fixed seeded subsets shared by every method and training seed.
Filter SMoLoRA upstream sequence to ScienceQA, TextVQA, GQA, VQAv2; image-bearing ScienceQA only.
Flatten released multi-turn training conversations into all individual human/assistant pairs before sampling.
Retain dataset-specific source scoring; never treat exact-match VQAv2 scores as official VQA consensus.
Cap greedy answers at 32 new tokens rather than the released inference launcher's 1024; selected references are short answers.
Use source training square-padding preprocessing consistently for train and eval; the released CL-MoE eval utility instead directly center-crops with CLIPImageProcessor.
